stages.title: Whole-number arithmetic
stages.hook: A shop has 347 red pens and 285 blue pens. Can you work out the total in your head, or at least say roughly how many without a calculator?
explain: Whole-number arithmetic uses four operations: add, subtract, multiply and divide. Place value is the key. In 347, the 3 means 3 hundreds, the 4 means 4 tens and the 7 means 7 ones.

When we add or subtract in columns we work from the ones, then tens, then hundreds. If a column is too big we carry. If we need more in a column we borrow (exchange) from the next column. Multiplying is repeated adding, and dividing is sharing equally or repeated taking away.
Estimating helps check answers. 347 + 285 is about 350 + 285, so a bit more than 600. If your answer is 932 you know to look again. When a sum has several operations, work out × and ÷ before + and −.

steps: Hundreds: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. The answer is 632, close to the estimate.

analogies.home: Adding up the cost of rice 347 and oil 285 at the market gives a bill of 632.
analogies.farm: A farmer has 6 rows with 14 plants each. 6 × 14 = 84 plants.
analogies.sport: 96 players are put into teams of 8. 96 ÷ 8 = 12 teams.
analogies.city: A bus has 52 seats. 3 buses carry 3 × 52 = 156 people.

stages.mnemonic: Ones, tens, hundreds, step by step. Estimate first and your checks will be kept.
terms: The value of a digit because of its position.
Moving extra tens (or hundreds) to the next column.
The rule for which part of a sum to do first.

misc.wrong: In 2 + 3 × 4 you do the sums from left to right, so the answer is 20.
misc.right: Multiplication comes before addition, so 3 × 4 = 12 first and then 2 + 12 = 14.

stages.limits: These methods are for whole numbers. Fractions, decimals and negative numbers need extra rules.

trip.prompt: Find a picture of an early counting tool and see how it showed place value.

questions.q: In the number 4 506, what does the 5 stand for?
questions.why: The digits are 4 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones.

questions.q: Which is the best estimate for 298 + 403?
What is 2 + 3 × 4?
questions.why: Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14.

questions.q: Why do we check by estimating?
o: It always gives the exact answer
It helps us spot big mistakes
questions.why: A rough answer shows if an exact answer is far off.

questions.q: Mina works out 500 − 178 and gets 478. How can you tell it is wrong without redoing it?
o: The answer is nearly 500, but we took away almost 200
questions.why: Taking away about 180 from 500 leaves about 320, not 478.

questions.q: Which operation undoes multiplying by 7?
questions.why: Division is the inverse of multiplication.

questions.q: Work out 500 − 178.
A school buys 6 boxes of 14 pencils. How many pencils?
Explain why 4 × 25 = 100 helps you find 8 × 25.
questions.model: 8 × 25 is double 4 × 25 because 8 is double 4. Double 100 is 200.
questions.why: Doubling one number doubles the product. 4 × 25 = 100, so 8 × 25 = 200.

questions.q: A shop sells pens in packs of 8. Dev needs 70 pens. How many packs must he buy so he has enough?
questions.why: 70 ÷ 8 = 8 remainder 6. 8 packs give 64, not enough, so he needs 9.

panel.q: Sam says 7 × 6 = 36 and so 7 × 7 = 43. What is the clear mistake?
o: One more group of 7 adds 7, so 7 × 7 = 49
panel.why: 7 × 7 = 7 × 6 + 7 = 42 + 7 = 49. Sam also had 7 × 6 wrong, it is 42.

panel.q: Why do we do multiplication before addition in 5 + 2 × 3?
panel.model: Multiplication is repeated addition, so 2 × 3 is a single chunk of 6. Everyone agrees on this rule so we all get 5 + 6 = 11.
panel.why: The rule is a shared agreement and fits with 2 × 3 meaning 3 + 3.

panel.q: An estimate for 49 × 21 is 50 × 20. What do we expect about the exact answer?
panel.why: 50 × 20 = 1 000 so 49 × 21 is near it. The exact answer is 1 029.

teach.model: Add numbers column by column from the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the ten to the next column. For example 47 + 35: 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 and carry 1, then 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 so the answer is 82.

points.ask: Where do I start adding?
What if a column adds up to more than 9?
How can I check the answer is sensible?

stages.title: Fractions and decimals
stages.hook: A pizza is cut into 4 equal slices and you eat 3. How could you write that as a fraction and as a decimal?
explain: A fraction describes part of a whole made of equal parts. In 3/4 the bottom number (denominator) says how many equal parts, and the top number (numerator) says how many we have. A fraction is also a division: 3/4 means 3 ÷ 4.
Equivalent fractions name the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 5/10. A decimal uses place value to the right of the point. 0.5 means 5 tenths, which is 5/10 = 1/2. 0.75 is 75/100 = 3/4.

To add fractions with the same denominator add the numerators: 1/4 + 2/4 = 3/4. With different denominators first change them to the same one: 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. To compare decimals line up the places: 0.7 is bigger than 0.07.

example.q: Find 2/5 of 20 and write 3/4 as a decimal.
steps: 2/5 of 20: divide 20 by 5 to get one fifth, 4.

analogies.home: Share a chapati in 4 equal parts. 3 parts is 3/4 or 0.75 of it.
analogies.farm: A field has 10 equal strips. 7 are planted: 7/10 or 0.7.
analogies.sport: A game has 2 halves. After the first half, 1/2 of the time has gone.
analogies.music: A whole note lasts 4 beats. A half note is 1/2 of that, 2 beats.

stages.mnemonic: Denominator is down below, it names the parts. Numerator is up on top, it counts the parts.
terms: The top number: how many parts we have.
The bottom number: how many equal parts make the whole.
Different fractions with the same value.
The dot separating whole numbers from parts.

misc.wrong: 1/3 is bigger than 1/2 because 3 is bigger than 2.
misc.right: The bigger the denominator, the smaller each part. 1/2 is bigger than 1/3.

trip.prompt: Look at the pictures of fractions and find one that matches 3/4.

questions.q: Which fraction is the same as 1/2?
questions.why: Doubling top and bottom keeps the value: 1/2 = 2/4.

questions.q: Which is the biggest?
questions.why: With the same top number, the smaller denominator gives bigger parts.

questions.q: Which decimal is the same as 3/10?
questions.why: Tenths are the first place after the point.

questions.q: Which is bigger, 0.7 or 0.07?
questions.why: 0.7 is 7 tenths and 0.07 is 7 hundredths.

questions.q: What is 1/4 + 2/4?
questions.why: Same denominator: add the tops and keep the bottom.

questions.q: Zuri says 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/8. What is her mistake?

Write 3/4 as a decimal.

questions.model: Divide the top and bottom of 3/6 by 3 to get 1/2. Both show the same share of the whole.

questions.why: Compare tenths first: 0.05 has 0 tenths, 0.2 has 2, 0.5 has 5, 0.75 has 7.

panel.q: Which statement is correct?
o: 2/3 is always bigger than 1/2 of anything
Fractions do not depend on the whole
2/3 of a small pizza can be smaller than 1/2 of a big pizza

panel.why: Fractions are parts of a whole, so the size of the whole matters when different wholes are compared.

panel.q: Mia says 0.30 is bigger than 0.3 because it has more digits. Is she right? Explain.
panel.model: She is wrong. 0.30 and 0.3 are equal because 3 tenths is 30 hundredths. A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value.
panel.why: Extra zeros at the end of a decimal add nothing. Compare place by place.

panel.q: What is 1/2 + 1/4?

teach.model: A fraction is part of a whole that is cut into equal parts. The bottom number tells how many equal parts. The top number tells how many we take. If a cake is cut into 8 equal slices and you eat 3, you ate 3/8.

points.ask: Do the parts need to be the same size?
What do the two numbers mean?
Can you show it with a pizza or cake?

stages.title: Percentages and ratios
stages.hook: A shop says "25% off". Another says "one quarter off". Which one is the better deal?
explain: Percent means "per hundred". 25% means 25 out of 100, which is 25/100 = 1/4 = 0.25. So 25% off and a quarter off are the same.
To find a percentage of a number you can use easy steps. 10% is one tenth, so divide by 10. 50% is a half. 25% is a quarter. For 20% of 80: 10% is 8, so 20% is 16.

A ratio compares amounts. A ratio of 2 : 3 means for every 2 of one thing there are 3 of the other. To share 20 in the ratio 2 : 3, there are 2 + 3 = 5 parts, each part is 20 ÷ 5 = 4, so the shares are 8 and 12.

example.q: A bag costs 50. It is 20% off. What is the new price?

analogies.home: A recipe uses 2 cups of rice to 3 cups of water, a ratio of 2 : 3. For 4 cups rice use 6 cups water.
analogies.farm: A farmer has 100 trees and 40 are mango trees. 40% are mango.
analogies.sport: A player scores 18 of 20 free throws. 18/20 = 90%.
analogies.city: A shop has 30% off a 200 coat, taking 60 off.

stages.mnemonic: Percent means out of one hundred. 10% is a tenth, 50% is half, 25% a quarter.
terms: A way to compare amounts, written like 2 : 3.
An amount taken off a price.
A part compared with the whole.

misc.wrong: A ratio of 1 : 3 means one third of the whole.
misc.right: 1 : 3 means 1 part to 3 parts, which is 4 parts altogether. So one quarter is the first part.

trip.prompt: Find a place on the page where percentages are used in the real world.

questions.q: Which is the same as 50%?
questions.why: 50 out of 100 is half.

questions.q: Which is the same as 25%?
What is 10% of 90?
questions.why: 10% is one tenth. 90 ÷ 10 = 9.

questions.q: The ratio of boys to girls is 1 : 2. What fraction of the group are boys?
questions.why: There are 1 + 2 = 3 parts, and boys are 1 of them.

questions.q: Which is a better score on a test?
A price rises by 10% and then falls by 10%. Compared with the start the price is...
questions.why: After +10% it is 1.1 times. Then 90% of that is 0.99 times, a bit less than the start.

questions.why: A quarter of 80 is 20.

questions.why: 5 parts, each 4. The larger share is 3 × 4 = 12.

Explain how you can find 15% of 60 using 10% and 5%.
questions.model: 10% of 60 is 6. 5% is half of that, 3. Add them: 6 + 3 = 9.

panel.q: Two shops: Shop A has 20% off 50. Shop B has 10 off 50. Which is cheaper?
panel.why: 20% of 50 is 10, so both take off 10.

panel.q: A drink mix uses squash and water in the ratio 1 : 4. Maya says there is 1/4 squash. Is she right? Explain.
panel.model: No. There are 1 + 4 = 5 parts in all, so squash is 1/5 of the drink, not 1/4.
panel.why: A ratio compares parts to parts. The fraction compares one part to the whole.

panel.q: A team won 12 of 20 games. Another won 15 of 30. Which won the greater percentage?

teach.model: Percent means out of 100. So 40% means 40 out of 100. To find 10% of a number, divide it by 10. To find 50%, halve it. For example, 10% of 70 is 7.

How do I find a percent of a number?

stages.title: Negative numbers
stages.hook: It is 3 degrees below zero in the morning. By afternoon it is 5 degrees warmer. What is the temperature now?
explain: Negative numbers are less than zero. We see them in temperatures below freezing, in money owed (debt) and in floors below ground. They sit to the left of zero on the number line.
The further left a number is, the smaller it is. So −5 is less than −2, and −2 is less than 1. A number and its opposite are the same distance from zero: 4 and −4.
To add, move right on the number line. To subtract, move left. −3 + 5: start at −3, go 5 right, and land on 2. −2 − 3: start at −2, go 3 left to −5.

example.q: The temperature is −3 degrees and rises by 5 degrees. What is it now?
steps: Draw a number line. Start at −3.
Rising means moving right. Count 5 steps: −2, −1, 0, 1, 2.

analogies.home: A freezer is at −18 degrees. The fridge is at +4.
analogies.city: In a lift, floor −1 is the level under the ground floor.
analogies.sea: A submarine at −50 metres is 50 metres below the sea surface.
analogies.tech: A phone account at −5 means you owe 5.

stages.mnemonic: Negatives live left of zero. Left is lower, right is higher, up the line is a hero.
terms: A line on which numbers are placed in order.
A number the same distance from zero on the other side.
A whole number, positive, negative or zero.

misc.wrong: −8 is bigger than −2 because 8 is bigger than 2.
misc.right: On the number line −8 is further left than −2, so it is smaller. −8 < −2.

trip.prompt: Find an example of negative numbers in daily life on the page.

questions.q: Which is the smallest?
questions.why: −7 is furthest left on the number line.

questions.q: Which is bigger, −4 or −9?
questions.why: −4 is nearer to zero, so it is bigger.

questions.q: What is 2 − 5?
questions.why: Start at 2, go 5 left to −3.

questions.why: −12 is furthest below zero.

o: She moved left instead of right
questions.why: Adding 2 moves right: −6 to −4.

questions.q: How far apart are −3 and 4 on the number line?
questions.why: 3 steps to zero and 4 more: 3 + 4 = 7.

questions.why: Further left means smaller.

questions.model: It goes from 2 to 0, which is 2 floors, then from 0 to −3, which is 3 floors. In total 5 floors.
questions.why: The distance between 2 and −3 is 2 + 3 = 5.

panel.q: A diver is at −8 metres and rises 3 metres. Where is she now?
panel.why: Rising moves to the right: −8 + 3 = −5.

panel.q: Why is subtracting a number from a smaller number allowed to give a negative answer?
panel.model: If you take away more than you have, you go below zero. For example 3 − 5 = −2, like owing 2.
panel.why: Negative numbers extend the number line so that taking away more than you have has an answer.

panel.q: If a bank account is −20 and 30 is paid in, what is the balance?

teach.model: Negative numbers are numbers less than zero. On a number line they are to the left of zero. For example, −3 degrees means 3 degrees below freezing. −5 is smaller than −2.

How can I picture them?
Where do we meet them in life?

stages.title: Basic algebra
stages.hook: A pattern of matchsticks makes squares: 1 square needs 4 sticks, 2 squares in a row need 7, 3 squares need 10. How many for 10 squares without drawing them?
explain: Algebra uses letters to stand for numbers. A letter like n can stand for any number in a pattern. 3n means 3 × n. An expression is a number sentence with letters, such as 3n + 1.
The matchstick pattern goes 4, 7, 10. It goes up by 3 each time, so the rule is 3 × n + 1, where n is the number of squares. For 10 squares: 3 × 10 + 1 = 31.
To substitute means to put a number in place of a letter. If x = 3, then 2x + 4 = 2 × 3 + 4 = 10. We can also simplify by collecting like terms: 2a + 3a = 5a, but 2a + 3b cannot be combined.

example.q: A rule is 3n + 1. Find the value when n = 4 and say what the 3 does.
steps: The 3 means the pattern grows by 3 each time n goes up by 1.

analogies.home: Each table seats 4 people, so n tables seat 4n people.
analogies.farm: Each cow has 4 legs, so n cows have 4n legs.
analogies.sport: Each team has 11 players, so n teams have 11n players.
analogies.city: A taxi costs 2 to start and 3 per kilometre: 3k + 2.

stages.mnemonic: A letter is a box that holds a number. Put the number in and work it out!

Numbers, letters and operations, without an equals sign.
Replace a letter with a number.
Terms with the same letter part, such as 2a and 3a.

misc.wrong: 3n means 3 and n written side by side, so n = 4 gives 34.

Simplify 2a + 3a.

questions.why: For n = 1: 3 + 2 = 5. For n = 2: 6 + 2 = 8. It fits.

questions.why: One example where the answers differ is enough to show two expressions are different.

Find 2x + 4 when x = 3.

questions.model: A variable is a letter that stands for a number, which can change or be unknown.
questions.why: Variables let us write rules that work for many numbers.

panel.q: Is 3n + 1 always an odd number when n is even?
panel.why: If n is even, 3n is even, and even + 1 is odd.

panel.q: A friend says "a + a = a²". Test with a = 3 and explain.
panel.model: a + a = 3 + 3 = 6, but a² = 9. They are different, because a + a = 2a, not a².
panel.why: Testing with numbers helps catch mistakes in algebra.

panel.q: Why is algebra useful?
o: It lets us write one rule for many cases
panel.why: A rule like 3n + 1 works for every n.

teach.topic: What a letter in algebra means
teach.model: In algebra a letter stands for a number we do not know yet or one that can change. For example n can be the number of tables, and 4n is the number of seats. If n is 3, there are 12 seats.

points.ask: What is the letter for?
What does it stand for?
Can you give an example?

stages.title: Equations and inequalities
stages.hook: A balance scale has a 7 g weight and a mystery weight on the left, and a 15 g weight on the right. It is perfectly level. How heavy is the mystery weight?
explain: An equation says two things are equal, like x + 7 = 15. To solve it we find the value of x that makes it true. The balance idea is: whatever you do to one side, do the same to the other.

Solve x + 7 = 15 by taking 7 from both sides: x = 8. Solve 3x = 18 by dividing both sides by 3: x = 6. For two steps, like 2x + 1 = 11, undo the adding first (x = 5 after 2x = 10), then the multiplying.

An inequality compares with <, >, ≤ or ≥. x > 4 means x can be any number larger than 4. We solve it in the same way, and the answer is a set of numbers. Always check by putting the answer back into the original.

analogies.home: A bill is 15 and you have paid 7. The rest, x, makes x + 7 = 15.
analogies.farm: 3 equal baskets hold 18 eggs. Each basket holds x, so 3x = 18.
analogies.sport: A runner needs more than 4 laps. Laps x > 4.
analogies.tech: A phone has 11% battery after being charged by 2% a minute from 1%: 2x + 1 = 11.

stages.mnemonic: Do the same to both sides and the scale stays level.
terms: A statement that two expressions are equal.
Find the value that makes it true.

misc.wrong: In an equation you can add to one side only.
misc.right: Whatever you do to one side you must do to the other, or the balance breaks.

trip.prompt: Find the picture of a balance and see how it models solving equations.

questions.why: Take 7 from both sides: x = 8.

questions.why: Inverse operations undo each other.

questions.why: 7 is greater than 4. 4 is not greater than itself.

questions.q: How many whole numbers greater than 0 satisfy x < 5?
questions.why: The numbers are 1, 2, 3, 4.

panel.q: Why does an equation like x + 7 = 15 have just one solution, while x + 7 > 15 has many?
panel.model: An equation says both sides are exactly equal, which only fits x = 8. An inequality allows any x above 8, so there are many answers.
panel.why: Equations pin down one value. Inequalities describe a range.

panel.q: The width w of a rectangle is x and its length is x + 3. The perimeter is 26. Which equation shows this?
panel.why: Perimeter is 2 widths plus 2 lengths. Solving gives 4x + 6 = 26, x = 5.

teach.model: An equation is like a balance. To find the unknown, do the same thing to both sides until the letter is alone. For example for x + 3 = 10, subtract 3 from both sides to get x = 7.

points.ask: What can I do to an equation?
How do I get the letter alone?
How do I know the answer is right?

stages.title: Geometry and angles
stages.hook: Why do the three corners of any triangle always add up to the same amount, even if the triangle looks very different?
explain: An angle measures a turn. We measure it in degrees. A full turn is 360°, half a turn (a straight line) is 180° and a quarter turn (a right angle) is 90°. Angles smaller than 90° are acute, and bigger than 90° but less than 180° are obtuse.

Rules help us find missing angles. Angles on a straight line add to 180°. Angles around a point add to 360°. The angles inside any triangle add to 180°, and inside any four-sided shape (quadrilateral) to 360°.

Why does a triangle add to 180°? If you tear the three corners off a paper triangle and put them side by side they make a straight line. This is a good check but not yet a proof; a proof uses parallel lines.

example.q: Two angles in a triangle are 50° and 60°. Find the third.

analogies.home: A door opens from closed to a right angle: 90°.
analogies.sport: A gymnast spins a full turn: 360°.
analogies.city: A road turns a corner at a right angle, 90°.
analogies.sea: A ship turns half a circle to go back, 180°.

stages.mnemonic: Straight is one-eighty, around is three-sixty, a corner is ninety and a triangle is one-eighty too.

misc.wrong: A bigger triangle has angles that add up to more than 180°.
misc.right: The size of the sides does not change the angle sum. Every flat triangle adds to 180°.

stages.limits: These rules are for flat surfaces. On a sphere, such as the Earth, the angles of a triangle add to more than 180°.

trip.prompt: Find the types of angle and match them to the pictures.

questions.why: A right angle is a quarter turn: 90°.

questions.q: How many degrees are on a straight line?
questions.why: A straight line is half a turn.

Explain why the angles of a triangle always add to 180° using the torn-corner idea.
questions.model: If you tear off the three corners and place them side by side with their points together, they make a straight line, which is 180°. This works for any triangle.
questions.why: The corners fit together into a straight line, so they sum to 180°.

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle two angles are equal and the third is 40°. What are the equal angles?
questions.why: 180 − 40 = 140, split in two: 70° each.

panel.q: Maya measures a triangle and gets 85°, 60° and 45°. What is likely?
panel.why: 85 + 60 + 45 = 190. A flat triangle adds to 180°, so a small measuring error is likely.

panel.q: Why must a triangle have at most one angle of 90° or more?
panel.model: The angles add to 180°. Two angles of 90° or more would already reach 180° or more, leaving nothing for the third angle.
panel.why: The 180° total limits how many large angles fit.

panel.q: A clock shows 3 o'clock. What is the angle between the hands?
panel.why: The hands point at 12 and 3, a quarter of a full turn.

teach.topic: Finding a missing angle in a triangle
teach.model: The three angles in a triangle always add up to 180 degrees. If you know two angles, add them and subtract from 180. For example, if two angles are 50 and 60, then 180 − 110 gives 70 degrees.

points.ask: What do the angles of a triangle add up to?
What do I do with the two angles I know?
Can you do an example?

stages.title: Area, perimeter and volume
stages.hook: You want to cover a floor with tiles and put a fence round a garden. Do these need the same measurement?
explain: Perimeter is the distance around the outside of a shape. Area is the amount of flat space inside. Volume is the amount of space inside a 3D shape. They use different units: cm or m for perimeter, cm² or m² for area, cm³ or m³ for volume.
For a rectangle, area = length × width and perimeter = 2 × (length + width). A rectangle 8 cm by 5 cm has area 40 cm² and perimeter 26 cm. A triangle has area = ½ × base × height.
A cuboid has volume = length × width × height. A box 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm holds 24 cubes of 1 cm. Two shapes can have the same perimeter and different areas.

example.q: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Find its area and perimeter.
steps: Different units: cm² for area, cm for perimeter.

analogies.home: Floor tiles cover an area. A skirting board goes round the perimeter.
analogies.farm: Fencing a field is perimeter. Planting seeds in it relates to area.
analogies.sport: A running track measures perimeter. Grass in the middle is area.
analogies.city: A water tank holds volume. A park sign shows area.

stages.mnemonic: Perimeter goes around the edge, area fills the floor, volume fills the room.
terms: Amount of flat space inside a shape, in square units.
Amount of space inside a 3D shape, in cubic units.

stages.title: Mean, median, mode and simple probability
stages.hook: A bag holds 3 red and 2 blue counters. Without looking you pick one. How likely is red, and how could you describe the typical number in a data set?
explain: The mean, median and mode are three ways to describe the middle of data. The mean is the total divided by the number of values. The median is the middle value when the data are in order. The mode is the most frequent value. The range is the biggest minus the smallest and shows the spread.
For 3, 5, 5, 8, 9 the total is 30, so the mean is 30 ÷ 5 = 6. The median is the middle one, 5. The mode is 5. The range is 9 − 3 = 6.

Probability tells how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Probability = favourable outcomes ÷ total equally likely outcomes. For 3 red among 5 counters, P(red) = 3/5. A fair die has P(even) = 3/6 = 1/2.

example.q: Find the mean and median of 2, 4, 4, 6, 9.
steps: Median: the data are in order. The middle (third) is 4.
Mode: 4 appears twice, so the mode is 4.
